validated_top_candidate.title: Tip- and Euler-depth-cluster-protected mid-segment flank-shadow de-jittering on d=2.8

validated_top_candidate.signature: Remove 100 m lateral digitisation-jitter shadow along interior mapped fault segments (d_cat <= 100 m AND d_end > 300 m AND cat_nbrs >= 2 AND d_euler > 300 m = 2,434 px on d=2.8), while explicitly preserving along-strike tip continuations (d_end <= 300 m: 1,360 px) and shallow Euler N=0 contact depth-cluster corroboration zones (d_euler <= 300 m: 143 px; 1,457 union protected pixels).
validated_top_candidate.why_missing_faults: Hermant et al. (2025, Fig. 2 & Fig. 9B) document up to 400 m lateral offsets between regional USGS Quaternary traces and 1 m LiDAR scarps. Along interior segments (cat_nbrs >= 2, d_end > 300 m) without an independent subsurface contact solution, a d_cat=100 m pixel is lateral digitisation halo on an already-mapped fault (0.0040 credit/FP, 4.8x below OOF break-even). At fault tips (d_end <= 300 m) or where a shallow Euler N=0 depth cluster corroborates a subsurface contact, the pixel marks an unmapped tip propagation or shallow buried splay (0.0092 credit/FP, 2.29x higher credit density).
validated_top_candidate.differs_from_repo: Prior H27-4 blindly pruned all 3,891 d_cat <= 100 m pixels on d=2.8 and was only shipped bundled with the now live-refuted T-v2 gap-closure dots (23ad46a4d7ba). Prior H31-1 fed Euler rasters into a 41-band GBDT and failed screen (-0.00195). This candidate uses retained SI=0 Euler depth clusters and catalogue tip geometry as a structural protection gate on d=2.8 with zero T-v2 drag.
validated_top_candidate.confounders: Catalogue-internal holdout overweights tip adjacency relative to isolated far-field faults; mitigated by reporting both H32-1 (protected) and solo H27-4 (unprotected) on d=2.8.
validated_top_candidate.cost: Low (~95 s CPU holdout + ~9 s GeoTIFF build); zero external downloads.

Its third finding is the important one: all three arms removed pixels at 0.101-0.140 credit per removed FP against a break-even of 0.019292, so the discarded pixels were worth 5-7x break-even. Remaining arms are therefore ranked ADD-first, and an ADD arm is validated on the far-field LOSFO harness (evidence/losfo_farfield_diagnostic.json), never on the interleaved holdout, which by construction holds out no off-catalogue habitat. addition_arm_validation_instrument.name: LOSFO far-field holdout
addition_arm_validation_instrument.why: The interleaved holdout hides catalogue components interleaved with the known catalogue, so 100% of its hidden truth lies at distance 0 from the published catalogue (evidence/arm_habitat_decomposition.json: habitat_A truth = 0 of 120,983 px). A shippable file may place no pixel on a catalogue cell, so that protocol contains no truth in the only habitat a submission can occupy and CANNOT validate an addition arm.
addition_arm_validation_instrument.frozen_gate_for_the_first_add_arm: added dots must beat credit/dot 0.0465 AND the inclusion threshold at the cell DTI, in >=3/4 folds and >=8/10 seeds
addition_arm_validation_instrument.caveat: held-out systems are still MAPPED faults, so this is an upper bound on performance against genuinely unmapped faults, not an estimate. Per-fold credit ratios span 0.876-1.204, so with 5 seeds effects smaller than ~+/-12% per fold are not resolvable.
